notes.text: Overnight bags only. The big suitcases are already on their way to Kujō House in Osaka, so pack today and tomorrow's clothes, swimsuits and chargers.
Check the wagyu is actually reserved at Aihara Meat Shop and the 8 Romancecar seats are booked together. If either isn't done, today's plan falls over.
Hakone in December is cold and gets dark early. Bring hats and gloves; the hills are brown and bare and the sculptures stand in winter light, not summer green.

stops.summary: Grab 8 Freepasses and the Romancecar seats, then raid the ekiben stands before boarding.
stops.story: This counter turns two days of mountain transport into one pass you just flash. The Freepass covers the Romancecar to Yumoto, the Tozan trains and buses, the ropeway and the pirate ship, plus discounts at the Open-Air Museum and Glass no Mori.
how: Find the Odakyu Sightseeing Service Center at the Odakyu west concourse.
Buy 8 two-day Freepasses from Shinjuku and pick up the Romancecar seats together.
Send two people for ekiben, coffee and beers while the rest queue.
tips: Keep the Freepass on you all weekend; you'll show it everywhere for the discounts.
The Romancecar platforms are a short walk away, so you don't need to rush the ekiben.
wishes: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.summary: Booked seats together, ekiben on your laps, and Tokyo fading into winter hills out the window.
stops.story: The Romancecar is Odakyu's showpiece express, and the 8 of you get booked seats together instead of standing on a commuter train. It's breakfast with a moving view, as Tokyo's endless suburbs thin out into the dark winter hills around Hakone.
how: Board at Shinjuku with the ekiben already in hand.
At Hakone-Yumoto, switch to the Hakone Tozan Railway: the 12:39 to Chokoku-no-Mori (on the Freepass).
tips: The Tozan line climbs by switchbacks, with the driver changing ends and the train reversing up the mountain. Grab a window.
Chokoku-no-Mori is the stop for both the gyoza and the museum.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Hakone's cult gyoza joint: cheese, natto, boiled, fried. Names on the board, beers on the table.
stops.story: Gyoza Center is the local institution that people still post about every week: dozens of styles, from pan-fried to boiled, cheese and natto, plus gyoza ramen. It's cheap, fast and loud, exactly what you want before a museum on a packed day.
how: Write the group's name on the board at the door. There are no reservations.
Wander Gora while you wait. Weekend lunch queues can run 30–60 min.
Order a spread across styles to share, plus beers all round.
tips: At busy times you may be split 4+4. Take it rather than waiting for one table of 8.
Last entry is 15:00 and it's closed Thursdays (not an issue today).
stops.booking: No reservations: names on the board at the door
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Giant sculptures on a cold hillside, a stained-glass tower to climb, and a footbath to warm your feet.
stops.story: This is a mountainside crowded with huge sculptures that you walk among rather than look at behind glass. In December the hills are bare and the light drops fast, which makes the stained-glass tower glow even more. Finish with your feet in the free footbath.
how: Show the Freepass at the ticket desk for the discount.
Climb the stained-glass tower first while there's still daylight outside.
End at the footbath, then catch the Tozan bus to Sengoku (Freepass).
tips: Closes 17:00, and it's dark early in December, so do the outdoor pieces first.
Reviewers who came in late afternoon found it uncrowded.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: The village butcher: pick up 2.4 kg of wagyu for tonight's cook-off before it shuts at 17:00.
stops.story: Aihara is the only proper butcher in Sengokuhara, a local shop known for its house 'Monjiro' roast beef and deli fry-ups. Tonight's cook-off runs on a local's wagyu, not supermarket packs.
how: One person collects the reserved order. Everyone else can head on to A-Coop.
If it wasn't reserved, ask for steak and yakiniku cuts for 8 and take what they have.
tips: CHECK: confirm the reservation by phone (0460-84-8429). The script: '12月19日（土）に和牛ステーキ／焼肉用を8人分、約2.4kg取り置きお願いします'.
Wagyu cuts run roughly ¥1,500-3,000/100 g. Ask the price when you call.
Fallback if it falls through: a Shinjuku depachika meat counter that morning, with ice packs.
wishes: Yunessun wine, sake and coffee baths in Hakone, and a villa wagyu cook-off on the Hakone night

stops.summary: The only supermarket for miles: load up on beer, sake, chuhai and breakfast before it closes at 18:00.
stops.story: A-Coop is Sengokuhara's only supermarket. That makes it tonight's bar, tomorrow's breakfast and the cook-off's side dishes all at once. It's cheap, and it sells out.
how: Split up: one pair on drinks, one on rice and veg, one on breakfast.
Buy more ice and drinks than you think you need. There's nowhere else to go later.
Get two taxis to the villa.
tips: Stock sells out, so don't count on the exact sake you want.

stops.summary: Wagyu cook-off: steak team vs yakiniku team, four judges with drinks, loser does the dishes.
stops.story: Two teams of two cooks each go head to head over a grill: one team does steak, the other does yakiniku. The other four judge, pour and heckle. This is the night people will still be arguing about years later.
how: Pick teams and a cooking order, then get the grill hot.
Judges score on taste, presentation and trash talk.
The losing team cleans up.
tips: Fridge the wagyu as soon as you check in.
Keep some meat back for tomorrow's breakfast rice bowls.
wishes: Yunessun wine, sake and coffee baths in Hakone, and a villa wagyu cook-off on the Hakone night

stops.summary: Your own hot spring in the cold mountain air, then a piano singalong. Get to bed before the early ropeway.
stops.story: The villa has its own hot spring, so the soak is just you eight, steam rising into the freezing dark. After that it's the piano and whatever the group can still sing.
how: Take turns in the villa onsen with drinks from A-Coop.
Piano singalong in the living room.
Call it at a sensible hour: the first ropeway is tomorrow morning.
tips: Don't drink much in the hot water; heat and alcohol hit harder together.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
